# skills

Reusable, boundary-agnostic Claude Code skills for engineering work, shipped as Claude Code plugins.

Skills live under `plugins/<plugin>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, one plugin per family, all listed in the `pleejr` marketplace at `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. A skill loads as `<plugin>:<name>` (`craft:scrutinize`). A machine that wants fewer skills enables fewer plugins. Work-specific skills live in a separate work-side marketplace, never here. `<skills clone>` means wherever this repo is cloned.

## Install

| Plugin | Carries | Hooks |
|---|---|---|
| `craft` | reasoning and verification skills; the shared output styles, as `craft:<style name>` | — |
| `infra` | Terraform, access and credential skills | — |
| `acronyms` | expand-acronyms | UserPromptSubmit |
| `herdr` | herdr-name, peer-sessions | SessionStart |
| `machine-config` | machine-config | SessionStart, SessionEnd |
| `plugin-updates` | plugin-updates: reports every installed plugin behind its latest release, from any marketplace, and offers the update | SessionStart |

A plugin that carries a hook wires it through its own `hooks/hooks.json`, so enabling the plugin is the wiring; nothing goes in `settings.json` by hand.

**Using the skills** — from GitHub, updated by Claude Code's own plugin refresh:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add pleejr/skills
claude plugin install craft@pleejr --scope user     # repeat per plugin
```

**Authoring them** — from your clone. A directory marketplace runs its plugins in place, so an edit is live in the next session and `git pull` is the update:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/pleejr/skills.git <skills clone>
claude plugin marketplace add <skills clone>
claude plugin install craft@pleejr --scope user
```

## Local config (`skill-config.env`)

A skill that needs an environment-specific value (a site, an org, an id) reads it from
`~/.claude/skill-config.env` (`KEY=value` lines; override the path with `$SKILL_CONFIG`),
resolved first-found-wins: CLI flag → env var → `skill-config.env`. That keeps this repo
generic. Secrets stay in their own chmod-600 files, never in this config.

## Shared output styles (`plugins/craft/output-styles/`)

Custom Claude Code output styles — hand-authored prose about *how to write* — ship in the
`craft` plugin. With `craft` enabled, Claude Code loads each one as `craft:<frontmatter name>`
(`craft:Briefing`), so `outputStyle` must name it that way. A machine without the plugin gets
them copied into `~/.claude/output-styles/` under their bare names by the `machine-config`
skill's `scripts/apply.sh`, which stands down for them once `craft` is enabled.

They are here rather than in a machine-config repo because that repo is **per boundary**: work
and personal each keep their own, and the two are never remotes of each other, so a style
published there can never reach the other laptop. This repo is already consumed from both, which
makes it the only store that crosses the gap.

```bash
# publish a style you wrote on this machine (does not commit; prints the commands)
MC="<skills clone>/plugins/machine-config/skills/machine-config/scripts"
"$MC/apply.sh" --promote Briefing
# ...or send it to the per-boundary config repo instead
"$MC/apply.sh" --promote Briefing --to config
```

Same boundary rule as everything else here, and **it is not mechanically enforced**: `apply.sh`
refuses a style carrying a home path or credential-shaped content, but an employer, a ticket key,
a colleague's name or an internal system has no shape to match on. Read the prose before you
commit it.

## Moving a machine off the old symlink install

Machines set up before the plugins linked skills into `~/.claude/skills/` with `bin/link.sh` and pulled at session start. Both are gone from this repo; the same steps apply on either boundary. Order matters where a legacy wiring refuses to change once its plugin is enabled.

1. **Unwire expand-acronyms first**, if the machine uses it: `<skills clone>/plugins/acronyms/skills/expand-acronyms/scripts/acronyms.sh unwire`. It refuses in plugin mode. Its mode and skip-list live in `~/.claude/skill-state` and carry over.
2. Add the marketplace and install the plugins (see [Install](#install)).
3. **Remove the old links and the sync:** every symlink in `~/.claude/skills/` pointing into the clone, `~/.claude/session-checks.d/pleejr-skills.sh`, and `~/.claude/skill-tags`.
4. **Legacy hooks:** `plugins/machine-config/skills/machine-config/scripts/install.sh` removes machine-config's SessionEnd hook and both `session-checks.d` drop-ins (with the plugin enabled it unwires instead of wiring). Delete a `settings.json` SessionStart entry running `herdr-name.sh session-start` by hand.
5. **Output styles:** `apply.sh --styles-only` (same directory) removes the copies it installed; rename `outputStyle` wherever it is set, from `Briefing` to `craft:Briefing`. A stale name falls back to the default style without a warning from Claude Code.
6. **Restart, then check:** each `<plugin>:` skill is listed once, `/output-style` lists the `craft:` styles once, and `scripts/verify.sh` reports every enabled plugin's hooks healthy.

## Repo tooling

`bin/pr-merge.sh` — merge a PR and clean up after it, safely from inside a linked worktree:

```bash
<skills clone>/bin/pr-merge.sh                      # PR of the current branch
<skills clone>/bin/pr-merge.sh --repo owner/name 27 # by number, in a named repo
<skills clone>/bin/pr-merge.sh 27                   # by number, in the repo the cwd belongs to
<skills clone>/bin/pr-merge.sh --dry-run
```

Repo-agnostic — run it from any repo, not just this one. **When you pass a number, pass `--repo` with it.** A bare number is resolved against whatever repo the cwd belongs to, so `pr-merge.sh 535` from the wrong directory is PR 535 of the wrong repo; this happened twice before the flag existed. With `--repo`, the cwd is irrelevant to the merge and local cleanup runs only when the cwd is a checkout of that same repo (otherwise the script stops after the API merge and says so). Without `--repo`, a numbered PR is refused when its head branch is not on the cwd repo's origin and its head repo is not the cwd repo — and a number that does not exist in the cwd repo fails with a hint to pass `--repo`. Note the limit of that guard: a PR fetched by number from the cwd repo is by construction a PR of that repo, so the guard cannot tell "you meant this repo" from "you meant another repo that happens to have a PR with the same number"; only `--repo` closes that case.

It exists because `gh pr merge --admin --delete-branch` **breaks under the worktree layout**: with the branch in a linked worktree and `main` held by the primary checkout, gh merges the PR server-side and then fails trying to switch the worktree to the default branch (`fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree …`). The merge succeeded, the error says otherwise, and gh aborts before deleting the branch — so the remote ref survives a run that claimed `--delete-branch`, and a later worktree of the same name is rejected non-fast-forward against a branch you believe is twice deleted.

The script merges through `--repo` (API only, no local git), confirms `MERGED` from the API rather than from an exit code, then deletes the remote branch, retires the worktree, deletes the local branch and fast-forwards the primary checkout — each step guarded by the state it expects, so re-running after a partial failure is the intended recovery. It keeps the worktree instead of removing it if the tree is dirty or its tip is not the merged commit, and leaves the primary checkout alone unless it is clean and sitting on the base branch.

## Boundary

The skills are boundary-agnostic and inherit the consuming vault's boundary/identity rules. This repo is consumed from **both personal and work** setups, so keep it strictly generic: **no work data, no secrets** ever committed here. That applies to `plugins/craft/output-styles/` as much as to skill code — it is prose, which is exactly where a ticket key or a colleague's name slips through unnoticed.
